Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book insights:

- FOMC remains hawkish (3.75–4.00% and “ongoing increases”), prioritizing a return to 2% inflation.
- October 2022 Beige Book indicates activity was flat to modest overall, with pronounced cooling in housing, mixed manufacturing, and softer discretionary retail; outlook turned more pessimistic. Labor markets stayed tight but showed early signs of easing; wage growth remained elevated. Price pressures were still widespread, with some input-cost relief.
- Beige Book also notes tighter credit conditions and softer loan demand in several categories, reinforcing SLOOS findings of broad tightening across C&I/CRE and consumer credit and weaker demand (autos, cards), with HELOCs an exception.
- These corroborate the Financial Stability Report’s downside skew (tighter financial conditions, housing slowdown, liquidity strains), pointing to a sharper deceleration in credit‑sensitive sectors than “modest growth” suggests. Offsets include resilient services spending and still-strong employment.

Net effect: downside risks to growth are higher than previously assessed; adjust sentiment modestly more negative.
